messages:
maria: Heads-up — enterprise customer `acme-inc` opened a ticket: their billing export API is returning 502 / huge latency. They sent a function-call payload. Investigating now.

maria: payload they sent (redacted keys):
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-function-1",
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Please export billing events from 2025-12-01 to 2026-02-28 as CSV" }],
  "function_call": {
    "name": "billing.events.export",
    "arguments": { "start_date": "2025-12-01", "end_date": "2026-02-28", "format": "csv" }
  }
}
```

maria: customer sees a 502 and says it takes >30s before error. They expect export to start and return a presigned URL.

raj: Can you paste the API request that hit our router? Any router logs?

maria: pasted router request header snippet:
```
POST /v1/functions/invoke HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
X-Request-ID: r-9f3a
Content-Type: application/json
```

maria: router log shows fuzzy match score 0.72 and it routed to `billing.report.generate` (internal name) instead of `billing.events.export`.

routing-bot: automated note — matched functions: [billing.report.generate (0.72), billing.events.export (0.68), billing.summary.fetch (0.21)]

lucy: uhoh. `billing.report.generate` is a heavy aggregation endpoint that scans 2+ years of data if format=csv, does on-the-fly joins, and streams a big report to internal blob storage. It hits the OLAP cluster and we've seen it spike latency.

oliver: why did the router prefer `report.generate`? the names/descriptions are similar?

raj: checking function metadata. Here are descriptions we currently ship:
```
- billing.events.export: \"Export raw billing events to CSV/JSON. Arguments: start_date, end_date, format\"
- billing.report.generate: \"Generate billing reports (summary/analytics) for date ranges. Arguments: start_date, end_date, format, granularity\"
```

lucy: both have `start_date`, `end_date`, `format` and both mention \"report/export\" in user-facing description. router's fuzzy matcher used the phrase \"export billing events\" and picked the higher-scoring function due to wording in `report.generate` doc that mentions \"billing\" and \"report\" more frequently in embeddings.

maria: customer provided the full function-call field (they explicitly requested `billing.events.export` in their function_call payload). Why did autorouter override that?

raj: good catch — two pathways: (1) model-generated function_call name (the LLM picks a function), and (2) router's final resolution that maps function names to canonical backend tools. We have a post-resolution step that validates args and sometimes remaps to a preferred internal op when signatures look compatible. The remapping logic incorrectly considers `billing.report.generate` compatible because of overlapping arg names.

lucy: repro steps I ran locally:
1) Send the exact payload maria pasted to `staging-router`
2) observe router decision: `report.generate` selected
3) router then invokes internal job queue; job payload contains `format: csv` and no `operation` flag, so `report.generate` does full aggregation and times out.

lucy: curl repro (staging):
```bash
curl -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/functions/invoke \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-function-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Export billing events 2025-12-01 to 2026-02-28 as CSV"}],"function_call":{"name":"billing.events.export","arguments":{"start_date":"2025-12-01","end_date":"2026-02-28","format":"csv"}}}'
```

lucy: result on staging: router selected `billing.report.generate`, job ran ~38s and returned 502 to client.

raj: root cause seems to be: remapping logic treats functions as compatible when their JSON-schema top-level field names are identical. We have no explicit intent discriminator.

maria: customer impact: export failed, they retried several times and triggered rate limits on their side. They want a fix + rollback plan.

oliver: short-term mitigation: disable remapping for billing namespace (hotfix) and add explicit match-wins for exact function_call.name if provided by client.

raj: agree. I'll push a fast fail: if incoming request includes an explicit `function_call.name`, the router must honor it and skip remap path. PR coming.

maria: can we also notify the customer and offer manual extract?

lucy: long-term: add an `intent` enum in schemas or require `operation` field for ambiguous tools (`export` vs `generate`) and tune text embeddings to penalize heavy ops for function-call suggestions. Also adjust router fuzzy threshold: require >0.85 to remap.

raj: created PR: https://git.internal/redwood/router/pulls/612 — sets `honor_explicit_function_call` default true and disables remapping for `billing.*` until 2026-03-25. Deploy green -> rollback path included.

maria: deploying patch to staging now, will test with the provided curl.

routing-bot: deploy started — staging router v1.14.8-hotfix (sha: a7c3)

lucy: tested against staging after deploy, now routing honors explicit `function_call.name` and returns 202 + presigned url job queued for `billing.events.export`. Verified customer payload returns quick 202.

maria: customer notified, manual CSV export queued and shared. They confirmed success.

oliver: follow-ups:
- (P1) update function descriptions to include explicit \"operation: export|generate\" examples
- (P2) add integration test that simulates explicit `function_call.name` and ensures router honors it
- (P3) telemetry: add metric `router.remap_count` and break down by namespace/tool

maria: marking as resolved from support side; thanks team :thumbsup:
